headline: 30-day ban and £215 fine: Ronaldo suspended after Portugal camp walkout
summary: The Portuguese FA punished the 41-year-old forward for intentionally breaching regulations after he abruptly left the squad's base in Copenhagen.
details: Cristiano Ronaldo has been handed a 30-day suspension and a £215 fine following an explosive walkout from the Portugal national team camp earlier this month.
The Portuguese FA’s disciplinary council ruled that the Al-Nassr forward intentionally breached Article 160(1) of their regulations.
The incident occurred on October 2, when Ronaldo left the squad's Copenhagen base on the eve of a Nations League match against Denmark.
The walkout followed a fallout with head coach Jorge Jesus after Ronaldo was an unused substitute against Norway and learned he would be omitted from the starting XI against Denmark.
Ronaldo accused Jesus of an "absolute breach of trust" in an open letter, though the manager denied making any agreements regarding the player's role.
Despite the conflict, Ronaldo apologized for abandoning his teammates and fans, stating that he deserved to be punished.
The veteran confirmed he is not retiring from international football as he continues to pursue a career goal total of 1,000.
Both coach Jorge Jesus and FA president Pedro Proença expressed their desire to welcome Ronaldo back once his punishment is served.
Ronaldo holds the world records for international goals (146) and appearances (234), having led Portugal to Euro 2016 glory.
caption:
A 30-day ban and a fine for the GOAT? Cristiano Ronaldo has been sanctioned by the Portuguese FA.

Cristiano Ronaldo has been handed a 30-day suspension and a £215 fine following an explosive walkout from the Portugal national team camp earlier this month.

The Portuguese FA’s disciplinary council ruled that the Al-Nassr forward intentionally breached Article 160(1) of their regulations.

The incident occurred on October 2, when Ronaldo left the squad's Copenhagen base on the eve of a Nations League match against Denmark.

The walkout followed a fallout with head coach Jorge Jesus after Ronaldo was an unused substitute against Norway and learned he would be omitted from the starting XI against Denmark.

Ronaldo accused Jesus of an "absolute breach of trust" in an open letter, though the manager denied making any agreements regarding the player's role.

Despite the conflict, Ronaldo apologized for abandoning his teammates and fans, stating that he deserved to be punished.

The veteran confirmed he is not retiring from international football as he continues to pursue a career goal total of 1,000.

Both coach Jorge Jesus and FA president Pedro Proença expressed their desire to welcome Ronaldo back once his punishment is served.

Ronaldo holds the world records for international goals (146) and appearances (234), having led Portugal to Euro 2016 glory.

headline: 187 killed in mob violence in nine months, HRSS report
summary: Mob deaths were more than double those from political clashes, according to the Human Rights Support Society.
details: At least 187 people were killed and 401 injured in 398 incidents of mob violence across Bangladesh in the first nine months of 2026, according to a Human Rights Support Society (HRSS) report.
The death toll from mob violence was more than two-and-a-half times the 73 deaths recorded in political clashes during the same period.
Mob violence incidents reportedly stemmed from allegations of theft, robbery, rape, and hurting religious sentiments, as well as attempts to establish dominance.
Political violence left 73 dead and 6,473 injured. Of these, 91 percent of incidents involved BNP infighting or clashes with rival parties.
BNP infighting alone accounted for 40 deaths and 2,632 injuries. Among the 73 killed in political violence, 46 were from the BNP, 8 from Jamaat-e-Islami, and 6 from the Awami League.
The report also recorded 657 rapes of women and girls, including 392 minors and 130 gang-rapes, with 29 women murdered after rape.
Other findings include 95 inmate deaths in jail, 518 journalists facing attacks or harassment, and 535 workplace deaths.
Additionally, 13 Bangladeshis were killed by BSF attacks along the Indian border and 8 died from landmines along the Myanmar border.
caption:
187 people killed in mob violence—more than double the deaths from political clashes in just nine months.

At least 187 people were killed and 401 injured in 398 incidents of mob violence across Bangladesh in the first nine months of 2026, according to a Human Rights Support Society (HRSS) report.

The death toll from mob violence was more than two-and-a-half times the 73 deaths recorded in political clashes during the same period.

Mob violence incidents reportedly stemmed from allegations of theft, robbery, rape, and hurting religious sentiments, as well as attempts to establish dominance.

Political violence left 73 dead and 6,473 injured. Of these, 91 percent of incidents involved BNP infighting or clashes with rival parties.

BNP infighting alone accounted for 40 deaths and 2,632 injuries. Among the 73 killed in political violence, 46 were from the BNP, 8 from Jamaat-e-Islami, and 6 from the Awami League.

The report also recorded 657 rapes of women and girls, including 392 minors and 130 gang-rapes, with 29 women murdered after rape.

Other findings include 95 inmate deaths in jail, 518 journalists facing attacks or harassment, and 535 workplace deaths.

Additionally, 13 Bangladeshis were killed by BSF attacks along the Indian border and 8 died from landmines along the Myanmar border.
